title: Array creation
description: Five ways to create an array — literal, Array constructor, Array.from, Array(n).fill, and Array.of.

notes: new Array(3) creates HOLES, not zeros — most array methods skip holes. Use .fill(0) or Array.from to populate.
Array(n).fill([]) shares ONE reference across every slot. For distinct sub-arrays use Array.from({ length: n }, () => []).
Array.of(7) is [7]; new Array(7) is length 7 with holes.

options: An array of length 3 with holes

questions.q: Why prefer Array.of(7) over new Array(7)?
options: Array.of pre-fills the slots with the passed value, while `new Array(7)` leaves them undefined
Array.of always treats args as values, even a single number
Array.of returns a frozen array, preventing accidental length mutation
Array.of's result is a typed array (Int32Array), giving constant-time numeric reads

exercises.prompt: Build [0, 1, 2, 3] with Array.from and a length-4 array-like.
exercises.template:
const a = Array.___({ length: 4 }, (_, i) => i);
console.log(JSON.stringify(a));
